concerns.text: Tasks T215, T216, and T217 mandate implementing experimental validation protocols (Stark-effect spectroscopy, dielectric spectroscopy) and external benchmarking against physical measurements. This directly violates spec.md Assumptions and FR-011 which explicitly state: 'Physical measurement validation is out of scope' and ground truth is restricted to 'QM9 quantum calculation reference data'.

Tasks T222, T223, and T224 require implementing conformational ensemble sampling (3-5 conformers per molecule) and weighted average predictions. This violates spec.md Assumptions which explicitly state: 'Single lowest-energy conformer per molecule... is used' and 'ensemble sampling is documented as future work'.

Tasks T211, T212, and T213 introduce physics-informed regularization and specific bond-angle/length filters based on external expert reviews not present in the spec. This constitutes scope creep that alters the defined 'lightweight SchNet-style GNN' architecture (FR-004) and adds unrequested validation logic not mandated by FR-001 through FR-013.

The entire Phase 8 (Review-Driven Enhancements) introduces significant computational complexity (ensemble sampling, physics-informed loss, external benchmark checks) without updating the hard constraints in FR-010 (6h runtime) and FR-013 (8GB memory). This creates a high probability of violating the spec's mandatory performance constraints.

Task T032 contains an unresolved claim status ('not_enough_info') regarding validation against QM9 reference data. This indicates the verification step for FR-011 (validating predictions against QM9 data) is not fully defined or completed, risking a failure to satisfy the mandatory requirement.
